title: Finite coefficient-root extension with an algebraically independent rooted tuple
statement: Let k→K be a field extension [def-pc-field-extension] in one universe, let s be a finite algebraically independent subset over k [def-weil-pbc-transcendence-basis], let p be prime with char(k)=p, and let P be any polynomial over E=k(s). There are fields l,L in that universe and commuting scalar towers k→l→L and k→K→L, with l/k and L/K finite purely inseparable [def-weil-pbc-finite-purely-inseparable-extension], and a finite algebraically independent subset t of L over l, such that E embeds in E₁=l(t), the embeddings E→K→L and E→E₁→L agree, every coefficient of P mapped to E₁ is a p-th power in E₁, and K together with E₁ generates L. No finiteness of K/E, finite generation of K/k, separability hypothesis, or degree inequality is assumed or asserted.

source.place: Algebra, Tag 04KM, coefficient-root construction in the induction step

proof.text: Put E=k(s). The set of quotients f(s)/g(s), for multivariate polynomials f,g over k with g(s) nonzero, is a subfield of K containing k and s. Conversely every such quotient lies in E. Hence every coefficient c of P has such an expression. For each of the finitely many nonzero coefficients choose one expression and put h=f g^(p-1), so c=h(s)/g(s)^p. Let C be the finite union of the coefficient sets of these h.

Fix an algebraic closure Ω of K. Every element of Ω has a unique p-th root: existence follows from algebraic closedness, uniqueness from injective Frobenius. Let l be the subfield generated over k by the roots of C, let t be the roots of s, and let L be the compositum of K and l(t) in Ω. All are actual subfields and belong to the same universe as K.

For a subfield F of Ω the elements z with z^p in F form a subfield, because Frobenius preserves sums, products and inverses. Applying this to F=k shows l^p is contained in k, and applying it to F=K shows L^p is contained in K. Thus l/k and L/K are purely inseparable. The constant roots and variable roots are algebraic, as roots of X^p-c. Their finite sets generate l/k and L/K, respectively, so the algebraic-generators lemma gives finiteness.

Put E₁=l(t) in L. Since each s_i=t_i^p, the original E embeds in E₁. These inclusions commute in L, giving the algebra structure E→E₁ and the scalar tower. For h=Σ c_I X^I, the element h̃=Σ c_I^(1/p) t^I belongs to E₁ and satisfies h̃^p=h(s). Consequently c=(h̃/g(s))^p in E₁. A zero coefficient is the p-th power of zero. This proves the coefficient condition for every index.

The root function gives a bijection between the finite sets s and t. If a nonzero polynomial G over l vanished on t, coefficientwise p-th powers would lie in k and would give a nonzero polynomial G^(p) over k on the same variables. It is nonzero by injectivity of Frobenius on l. Its evaluation on s equals G(t)^p=0, contradicting algebraic independence of s. Thus t is algebraically independent over l. Finally K and E₁ generate L by its compositum construction; equivalently adjoining the range of K→L over E₁ is top.

theorem exists_coefficientRoot_extension
    (k K : Type w) [Field k] [Field K] [Algebra k K]
    (s : Finset K)
    (hs : AlgebraicIndependent k ((↑) : s → K))
    (p : ℕ) [Fact p.Prime] [CharP k p]
    (P : (IntermediateField.adjoin k (s : Set K))[X]) :
    ∃ (l : Type w) (hl : Field l) (akl : Algebra k l)
      (L : Type w) (hL : Field L) (aKL : Algebra K L) (alL : Algebra l L)
      (akL : Algebra k L) (htl : IsScalarTower k l L) (htK : IsScalarTower k K L),
      Module.Finite k l ∧ IsPurelyInseparable k l ∧
      Module.Finite K L ∧ IsPurelyInseparable K L ∧
      ∃ t : Finset L, AlgebraicIndependent l ((↑) : t → L) ∧
        ∃ (a : Algebra (IntermediateField.adjoin k (s : Set K))
            (IntermediateField.adjoin l (t : Set L))),
          IsScalarTower (IntermediateField.adjoin k (s : Set K))
            (IntermediateField.adjoin l (t : Set L)) L ∧
          (∀ n : ℕ, ∃ b : IntermediateField.adjoin l (t : Set L),
            algebraMap (IntermediateField.adjoin k (s : Set K))
              (IntermediateField.adjoin l (t : Set L)) (P.coeff n) = b ^ p) ∧
          IntermediateField.adjoin (IntermediateField.adjoin l (t : Set L))
            (Set.range (algebraMap K L)) = ⊤
